summary: Top AI leaders, including Sam Altman and Demis Hassabis, signed a statement warning that AI poses an extinction risk comparable to pandemics and nuclear war. The article questions whether society is taking this threat seriously enough and highlights calls for regulation.

claims.text: Hundreds of AI scientists and researchers signed a one-sentence open letter stating that mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority.
claims.evidence_quote: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war

claims.text: The letter was signed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis.
claims.evidence_quote: including OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman and Google DeepMind chief executive Demis Hassabis

claims.text: Dan Hendrycks, executive director of the Center for AI Safety, compared the warnings to atomic scientists' warnings about nuclear weapons.
claims.evidence_quote: reminiscent of atomic scientists issuing warnings about the very technologies they’ve created

claims.text: Hendrycks quoted Robert Oppenheimer: 'We knew the world would not be the same.'
claims.evidence_quote: We knew the world would not be the same.

claims.text: The article argues that industry leaders are pleading for policymakers to establish regulations before it is too late.
claims.evidence_quote: They are pleading for policymakers to erect some guardrails and establish baseline regulations to defang the primitive technology before it is too late.

claims.text: The statement was released on Tuesday, May 30, 2023.
claims.evidence_quote: On Tuesday, hundreds of top AI scientists, researchers, and others
